Optimal.Notes: At 8 W TDP the Deck handles this lightweight game at native 1280x800 with medium-to-high visuals and a smooth 60 fps in typical scenes. Drop particle and shadow quality if you plan to run large-scale physics experiments.

profiles.Summary: People Playground is a lightweight 2D sandbox/ragdoll physics game with very modest PC requirements, making it an excellent fit for the Steam Deck at native resolution and high frame rates. ProtonDB reports trend platinum, suggesting it runs smoothly under Proton with little to no configuration needed.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck or ProtonDB detail reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very modest 2D/physics-sandbox PC requirements and the Deck's hardware. On first run, confirm Proton launches correctly and check frame rate during a busy scene with many ragdolls — if it dips below your cap, reduce Particle Quality first, as that is the primary GPU cost in this game.

MaxBattery.Notes: This 2D physics sandbox is extremely light on the GPU; a 5 W TDP and low GPU clock are more than sufficient for simple to moderately complex scenes. Battery life will be excellent in typical play, though spawning hundreds of ragdolls will stress the CPU regardless of these settings.

KnownIssues: The game's open-ended sandbox nature means complex scenes with many ragdolls, explosions, or physics interactions can tank frame rates regardless of settings — this is a CPU/physics bottleneck, not a GPU one.
No native Linux build; runs via Proton, but gold/platinum reports indicate this is generally seamless.
Controller/gamepad support is not officially stated; mouse and keyboard via the Deck's trackpad and on-screen keyboard may be required for full functionality.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With no TDP or GPU cap the Deck runs this 2D sandbox at max visual fidelity with a rock-solid 60 fps in normal play; the game's own physics simulation is the real ceiling, so frame drops in chaotic scenes are expected and unavoidable regardless of GPU settings.

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at medium quality gives a clean, sharp image well-suited to the OLED screen; 7 W TDP is ample for typical sandbox play and leaves headroom when physics loads spike.

profiles.Summary: People Playground is a lightweight 2D physics sandbox that runs natively well below the Steam Deck's hardware ceiling, easily hitting 60 fps at native resolution with minimal power draw. Performance scales with the number of ragdolls and active simulations, so complex scenes can tax the CPU more than the GPU.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB-specific performance reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very lightweight PC requirements (DX10, 2 GHz CPU, 4 GB RAM), its 2D physics-sandbox nature, and the Deck hardware. On first run, check fps during a busy ragdoll scene — if it holds 60 fps easily at Optimal, try Max Performance; if it struggles, lower particle and lighting quality first.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 4 W TDP with a low GPU clock, even busy scenes stay within budget; the main threat to the frame cap is CPU physics load from large ragdoll piles, not the GPU. Drop the ragdoll count if the cap is broken.

KnownIssues: Complex scenes with many ragdolls and active physics objects can cause significant CPU-side frame drops regardless of GPU settings.
The game's own developer notes it 'offers enough freedom to be able to slow down any computer' — heavy sandboxes may dip below target fps.
No native Linux build confirmed; Proton (Gold/trending Platinum) is required and may add minor overhead.
Controller/gamepad support is not officially listed, so on-screen keyboard or touchscreen may be needed for some UI interactions.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With no TDP cap the Deck's APU can boost freely to sustain 90 Hz in simple scenes; expect drops into the 50s during heavy ragdoll chaos as the CPU becomes the bottleneck, not the GPU.
